_comment: REAL data. v1 slice 1: the 10 water and sewerage companies filing an EDM storm-overflow annual return in England, with their 2025 spill totals. Slice 2: the 16 power-generating account holders with the largest UK ETS verified emissions in 2025, absolute tonnes only (intensity unknown, see the README). Slice 3: the 16 oil and gas account holders (extraction and refining) with the largest UK ETS verified emissions in 2025, on the same terms. Slice 4: the 16 heavy-industry account holders, on the same terms. Slice 5: the 16 UK-incorporated aircraft operators, on the same terms; the UK ETS covers only domestic and European flights, so long-haul emissions are not in these figures. Slices 6 and 7: the oil and gas and heavy-industry holders ranked 17 to 32, on the terms of slices 3 and 4. Slice 8: the 16 food and drink account holders, on the same terms. Slice 9: the power holders ranked 17 to 32, on the terms of slice 2. Slice 10: the 12 largest holders with an installation outside every earlier filter, each counted whole: gas networks, heat and steam, manufacturing and the rest of heavy industry. Provenance, reconciliation and caveats are in data/README.md. Storm overflows are permitted to spill in rainfall: an EDM spill is a recorded discharge, not by itself a breach.
